text:
liam: Heads-up — our int4 canary (fresh quantized build) is showing a strange double-invoke pattern on tool calls. Not a parsing failure per se, but downstream gets two identical func calls for ~3% of requests.
sarah: Seen similar in a small subset of mirrored traffic earlier today. Looks like retry+stream reassembly interacting with our call adapter.
guillermo: Important: are both invokes identical payloads and identical ids?
liam: Payloads match byte-for-byte, but request_id differs. example log: 
```
2026-02-18T14:21:03Z INFO invoke tool_start id=abc123 quant=int4 request_id=r1
2026-02-18T14:21:03Z INFO invoke tool_start id=abc123 quant=int4 request_id=r2
2026-02-18T14:21:03Z INFO tool_return id=abc123 status=ok
```
No downstream duplicate returns though — usually only one result consumed.
anya: That smells like our retry budget kicking in while the streaming generator is still producing function call tokens. If client-side ack is slow we reissue, but the model later emits the call again.
sarah: Right — and in int4 canary we've been seeing longer first-call latency in ~0.8% of traces due to KV-cache warm-up. That could trip timeout-based retries.
guillermo: Could also be that the structured output parser doesn't canonicalize whitespace/control chars; two streams reconstruct to slightly different tokenization and our dedupe check (which is strict equality on request_id) misses it.
liam: Repro snippet from mirror run (sanitized):
```
# payloads received by call-adapter
{"tool":"lookup","args":{"q":"foo"},"__raw_stream_summary":"func_call @t=0..34"}
{"tool":"lookup","args":{"q":"foo"},"__raw_stream_summary":"func_call @t=0..62"}
```
Same semantic call but different chunk boundaries.
anya: Proposed mitigation: make call-adapter dedupe tolerant by computing a stable semantic fingerprint (tool name + canonicalized args) instead of relying on request_id. Also increase idempotency token lifetime for in-flight streaming requests.
sarah: Also add a quick post-parse repair pass that normalizes trailing commas and common escape variants before matching. Many of the double-invokes come from streaming boundary replays that introduce extra whitespace/newline tokens which break equality.
guillermo: Agreed. We should triage with a focused AB test: enable fingerprint dedupe on 1% of canaries and run mirror traffic for 4 hours. If it reduces duplicate invokes to <0.2% we can roll.
liam: Can someone produce the small eval harness? Need: sample of 10k mirrored sessions, labels where duplicate-invoke observed, and a diff metric (duplicates per 1k requests). Also record tokenization deltas and first-call emission latency.
anya: I can wire a harness to the mirror pipeline tomorrow. Will add telemetry buckets: emit_metric("duplicate_invoke", 1) with tags {quant, model, canary}.
sarah: Also let's capture full raw stream chunks for ~100 representative failures (store off-cluster for privacy). That will let us try different canonicalizers.
guillermo: Quick safety: ensure dedupe fingerprint doesn't suppress legitimate retries that carry different args. Use a heuristic: fingerprint + timestamp window (e.g., same fingerprint within 5s => dedupe).
liam: Ops-bot: kick a canary roll with dedupe-prototype flag for model raven-int4-canary if infra is green.
ops-bot: @liam Requested: start canary raven-int4-canary with flag dedupe_prototype=true for 1% traffic. Deployment queued.
liam: One more observation — when adapters attempt JSON-repair heuristics we sometimes end up inserting a missing closing brace which masks the original streaming boundary issue. That can hide the upstream root cause. Keep raw logs until we validate the repair approach.
sarah: Good point. Add a toggle to store both raw and repaired payloads in the sample bucket.
guillermo: Long-term fix idea: move idempotency token generation into the server runtime so it's preserved across retries and mirrors. That will make dedupe by idempotency viable again.
anya: For short-term, I'll implement stable fingerprint dedupe + increased retry window. Will run the 1% AB for 12 hours and post numbers.
liam: Plan of record:
- anya runs 1% canary with fingerprint dedupe (start 12:00 UTC tomorrow)
- sarah collects 100 raw+repaired failure artifacts
- guillermo defines fingerprint algorithm and review CL by EOD
- liam will draft postmortem template in case rolling change causes regressions (quality or latency)
If anything looks bad, abort. :ok_hand:
sarah: Adding checklist item — validate that downstream tool servers handle duplicate tool_start gracefully (idempotent ops).
liam: Thanks team. If AB reduces duplicates significantly we can bake into release. Otherwise fallback to runtime idempotency work.
anya: Will update thread with initial metrics after first 500k mirrored requests.
liam: Closing for now.
